passwordResetPage.title: AuthCoreService Password Reset
passwordResetPage.description: Use the emailed reset link or paste the reset token to set a new password.

ep_signup.developerNotes: Signup creates only regular USER accounts. Role and RBAC are fixed to least-privilege defaults and cannot be elevated from request payload.

documentation.summary: Create a new least-privilege USER account through the public signup flow.
documentation.description: This is the public self-service account creation route for the auth example. The handler ignores any attempt to elevate the role beyond USER.

sections.title: Authorization
sections.body: Public route. No bearer token is required.

sections.title: Request Contract
sections.body: Supply `username`, `email`, and `password`. Optional `profile` data is stored with the created user. The role and RBAC grants are fixed to USER-safe defaults regardless of client input.

sections.title: Responses
sections.body: Returns `201` on success, `409` when the username already exists, and `400` when required fields are missing.

sections.title: Operational Notes
sections.body: Passwords are hashed before storage and the created account is persisted into `auth_users`.

ep_signin.developerNotes: Production-ready signin script: accepts username or email, verifies hashed credentials, and issues bearer tokens with sessionVersion for global revocation control.

documentation.summary: Authenticate with username or email and receive a bearer token.
documentation.description: The auth example accepts either a username or an email address and returns a JWT plus the resolved claim set.

sections.title: Authorization
sections.body: Public route. No bearer token is required.

sections.title: Request Contract
sections.body: Provide `username` or `email` and `password`. `identifier`/`login` can be used as a single-field alias and are resolved into username or email automatically.

sections.title: Responses
sections.body: Returns `200` with `token`, `accessToken`, and JWT claims on success. Invalid credentials return `401`.

sections.title: Operational Notes
sections.body: The script reads the session control record and embeds `sessionVersion` so sign-out-all and password resets can revoke older tokens globally.

ep_me.developerNotes: Loads the authenticated user from auth_users, checks auth_session_controls for the effective session version, and returns the current user profile only.

documentation.summary: Return the currently authenticated user profile.
documentation.description: This protected auth example route returns the normalized user profile for the current authenticated subject.

sections.title: Authorization
sections.body: Bearer authentication is required.

sections.title: Request Contract
sections.body: No request body or query parameters are required. The route reads the authenticated subject from `params.auth`.

sections.title: Responses
sections.body: Returns the normalized user profile merged from `auth_users` for the current authenticated subject.

sections.title: Operational Notes
sections.body: Reads auth_session_controls to resolve the effective session version before returning the current authenticated user profile.

ep_forgot_password.developerNotes: Forgot-password flow using jwt + email VI modules. Every issued reset token is persisted with its expiry and can only be used once.

documentation.summary: Generate a password-reset token and email a reset link to the matching user.
documentation.description: This route resolves the target user by username, email, or a combined `identifier` field, then signs a short-lived reset token.

sections.title: Authorization
sections.body: Public route. No bearer token is required.

sections.title: Request Contract
sections.body: Provide either `username`, `email`, or `identifier`. When SMTP is configured, the service sends an email; otherwise it still returns the generated reset link for testing. Each generated token is recorded server-side with a strict expiry.

sections.title: Responses
sections.body: Returns `200` with the generated `resetLink` when a matching user exists. Missing users return a route-level error payload.

sections.title: Operational Notes
sections.body: The reset link now lands on a browser-safe GET page at `/reset-password?token=...`, which posts the new password back to the same endpoint. The token is stored as a one-time credential and is consumed after a successful reset.

ep_reset_password.developerNotes: Reset route validates password-reset JWTs, requires a matching stored one-time token record, consumes it, updates the password hash, and revokes every existing bearer token for that user.

documentation.summary: Validate the password-reset token, change the password, and revoke all existing bearer sessions.
documentation.description: The auth example supports both a browser GET form and the POST JSON API for completing password resets.

sections.title: Authorization
sections.body: Public route. A password-reset token is required instead of a bearer token.

sections.title: Request Contract
sections.body: Submit `token` and `newPassword`. Browser users can open the emailed GET link, paste or keep the token, and submit the new password from the built-in form.

sections.title: Responses
sections.body: Returns `200` when the password hash is updated and the user session version is incremented. Invalid, expired, mismatched, or already-used reset tokens return `400` and missing users return `404`.

sections.title: Operational Notes
sections.body: Successful resets consume the stored one-time token, update `passwordHash`, blank any legacy plaintext password, and revoke every previous bearer token by rotating `sessionVersion`.

ep_users_read.developerNotes: Read route forwards the supplied VDB query as-is. `{}` therefore means all users for privileged callers, while regular users must explicitly query their own username or email.

documentation.summary: Read auth user records using the supplied VDB query object.
documentation.description: The query object is forwarded to VDB as-is. `{}` therefore means “match all users”, not “current user only”.

sections.title: Authorization
sections.body: Bearer authentication is required. ADMIN and SUPER_ADMIN can query any matching users. Regular USER accounts must explicitly target their own username or email in the query.

sections.title: Query Behavior
sections.body: The route uses `req.query` directly. Empty query objects such as `{}` return every matching user only for privileged actors. Regular users receive `403` unless the query explicitly scopes to their own username or email.

sections.title: Responses
sections.body: Returns `200` with `users`, `count`, `query`, and `requestedBy`. If a non-empty query matches nothing the route returns `404`.

sections.title: Operational Notes
sections.body: The response always includes an array so list and filtered lookups use the same shape. When exactly one record matches, `user` is also populated with the first entry for convenience.

ep_users_update.developerNotes: Update route forwards the supplied VDB query as-is after RBAC validation. Regular users must explicitly target their own username or email; admins can update any matched users.

documentation.summary: Update one or more auth user records using the supplied VDB query object.
documentation.description: The query object is forwarded to VDB as-is after RBAC validation. Privileged users can update any matching users; regular users must explicitly target their own username or email.

sections.title: Authorization
sections.body: Bearer authentication is required. Regular USER accounts can only change their own profile data and password. ADMIN cannot edit SUPER_ADMIN accounts, and only SUPER_ADMIN can assign ADMIN or SUPER_ADMIN roles.

sections.title: Query Behavior
sections.body: The route no longer treats `{}` as an own-profile shortcut. `{}` means “all matching users”, so only privileged actors may use it. Use the query object to select records; `body.username` is rejected.

sections.title: Mutation Rules
sections.body: Allowed body fields are `email`, `profile`, `password`/`newPassword`, `role`, and `rbac` subject to RBAC checks. Password changes rotate the session version for every matched user.

sections.title: Responses
sections.body: Returns `200` with `users`, `count`, and the raw VDB update result when the update succeeds. No matches return `404` and revocation failures are surfaced as `500` after the data update has occurred.

ep_users_delete.developerNotes: Delete route forwards the supplied VDB query as-is after RBAC validation and pre-delete session revocation. Regular users must explicitly target themselves.

documentation.summary: Delete auth user records selected by the supplied VDB query object.
documentation.description: The query object is forwarded to VDB as-is after RBAC validation and pre-delete session revocation.

sections.title: Authorization
sections.body: Bearer authentication is required. Regular USER accounts must explicitly target their own username or email. ADMIN cannot delete SUPER_ADMIN accounts.

sections.title: Query Behavior
sections.body: `{}` means “delete all matching users” and is therefore reserved for privileged actors. The route first resolves every matched row, validates RBAC, revokes sessions, and only then runs the delete operation.

sections.title: Responses
sections.body: Returns `200` with `usernames`, `count`, and revocation metadata when the delete succeeds. No matches return `404`, and any failed session revocation returns `500` before the delete runs.

sections.title: Operational Notes
sections.body: Every matched user has `auth_session_controls.sessionVersion` incremented so existing bearer tokens are invalidated before the user documents are removed.

ep_register_admin.developerNotes: Register route requires bearer auth. SUPER_ADMIN can create ADMIN/USER/APPLICATION; ADMIN is restricted to USER/APPLICATION and receives explicit 403/409 failure responses.

documentation.summary: Create ADMIN, USER, or APPLICATION accounts through the protected register route.
documentation.description: The register route is intended for administrative provisioning, not public signup.

sections.title: Authorization
sections.body: Bearer authentication is required. SUPER_ADMIN and ADMIN may call the route, but only SUPER_ADMIN may create ADMIN users. The route never creates SUPER_ADMIN accounts.

sections.title: Request Contract
sections.body: Provide `username`, `email`, `password`, and optionally `profile`, `role`, and `rbac`. The default example in the docs now provisions an ADMIN account because that is the main administrative use-case.

sections.title: Responses
sections.body: Returns `201` on success, `409` when the username already exists, and `403` when the requested role is not permitted for the caller.

sections.title: Operational Notes
sections.body: Passwords are hashed before storage and the created record is persisted into `auth_users` with `createdBy` set to the authenticated actor.

ep_signout_all.developerNotes: Revokes all active sessions for the authenticated user by incrementing sessionVersion in auth_session_controls. `exclude_current_session=true` preserves only the current bearer token hash; every older token becomes invalid across protected services.

documentation.summary: Revoke every bearer token for the current authenticated user.
documentation.description: This route increments the session version for the signed-in user and optionally excludes the current token.

sections.title: Authorization
sections.body: Bearer authentication is required.

sections.title: Request Contract
sections.body: Optional body flag `excludeCurrentSession`/`exclude_current_session=true` keeps the current token alive, but only when the current bearer token can be hashed and persisted.

sections.title: Responses
sections.body: Returns `200` with the next session version and revocation metadata when the session-control record is saved successfully.

sections.title: Operational Notes
sections.body: Downstream services validate `sessionVersion`, so every previously-issued bearer token becomes invalid as soon as the control record is updated.
